accuracy.evidence: Checked against the national curriculum in England, English Appendix 1 Years 5–6 (words with silent letters: doubt, island, lamb, solemn, thistle, knight; some letters were sounded hundreds of years ago) and the Oxford English Dictionary / Online Etymology Dictionary histories: Old English cniht, wrītan, lamb and gnætt sounded k, w, b and g; the b in doubt was added after Latin dubitare and the s in island after isle, so the lesson says these were never said in English. Every relative was checked for the sounded letter: signal, muscular, autumnal, bombard, crumble, hymnal; signing, muscles and autumns keep the letter silent.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the real slips: spelling by sound alone (thum, rite, dout, nife: OOPS, GAP, challenge q1 and q5, p5), silent letter in the wrong place (kne, whrist), treating an inflected form as a helpful relative (signing, muscles, autumns in KIN and m6), homophone confusion (knight/night, muscle/mussel, hymn/him: KIN distractors, OOPS 3, m7), thinking every silent letter was once said (challenge q4, m4), and mixing up the kn/gn/wr/mb families (SORT, challenge q6).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagquiet is built on the gap between letters and sounds: a word split into letter tiles with its spoken form shown so the learner taps the letter that makes no sound, a word card dragged into kn / wr / gn / mb family bins, a pick of the relative where the letter is heard, a letter tile dragged into the gap of a word, and a sentence slip finder. flagexcept (tricky words) and flagorigin (Greek/French/Latin patterns) teach different mechanisms; lab_distinct gate is 9% or less against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The rules come out of the feedback: tapping n in knot returns 'You can hear the n in "not"'; putting knock in wr returns 'knock has no wr'; choosing signing returns 'signing is the same word with an ending. The g is still silent'; choosing column for autumn says it sounds alike but is not in the family; dragging w into _nife says that is not how it is spelt and lists the families.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options the tasks disprove: 'yes, a soft k sound' for knot (HEAR 1 shows it sounds like not), 'the m' for climb (SORT puts climb in mb with a silent b), and 'no, that g is always silent' for sign (KIN 1 finds signal). A.reveal names the locked-in pick when each task ends.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with twelve wrong-answer messages naming the slip: knee starts with a silent k, you need the k and two e letters, you hear both b sounds in bump, you hear the b in robin, signing keeps the g silent, sighed is not in the family, nobody said the b in doubt, it was added on purpose to match the Latin, wrist starts with wr, wrist has wr not whr, gnome starts with g not k, and the silent letter is at the start.

readability.evidence: learn/readability.py: kid FK grade 1.3 (family limit 5.0), adult 6.4 (limit 10.0). Kid paragraphs use short sentences and one example pair each (knot/not, knit and gnat, sign and signal). Canvas prompts are one sentence; each piece of feedback is one or two.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs cover what a silent letter is, the four families, why the letters are there and the word-family trick. Adult text gives the Years 5–6 appendix statement, which letters were lost from speech and which were added by scholars, named mistakes including inflected forms and homophones, and what the lab does. Content gate found no filler; explanation under 12% similar to every other lesson including 782 tricky words and 797 Greek/French/Latin spellings.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px screenshots in light and dark for all six steps plus a wrong-answer state on each task (n tapped in knot, knock in wr, signing chosen, w in _nife, cut tapped). Letter tiles are at least 52 px wide for six-letter words, family bins 70 px tall, and the dragged card follows the finger without leaving the canvas. Walkthrough passed on iPhone 13 and desktop.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag and tap has a button twin below the canvas: one per letter ('Letter 1, k, is silent'), one per family ('Put knock in the kn family'), one per relative, one per letter for the gap ('Put k in the gap'), and one per word in the slip sentence. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after every action, the challenge feedback is a role=status live region, warnings switch to #fda4af on dark, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
